newsitem.title: INDIA: India Birla income fund sets 6-mth div at 8.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: India Birla income fund sets 6-mth div at 8.0 pct.

text.p: Birla Income Plus, India's largest private sector open-ended mutual fund, set a dividend of 8.0 percent for the six months ended March 31, 1997, chief executive of Birla Capital International AMC said on Wednesday.
The fund had paid 16.5 percent for the period October 1995 to September 1996, its first operational year.
"We have maintained the dividend," Ramamoorthy Ganesh, chief executive officer of Birla Capital International AMC Ltd, investment manager to Birla Mutual Fund, told Reuters.

"But there is a bit of a caution - it will be difficult to match this kind of of performance in a falling interest scenario," he said, referring to a fall in Indian interest rates beginning the second half of April 1997.
"It's a turning point. We have announced the dividend when interest rates, short-term and long-term, are falling," he said.

Indian banks and term lending institutions have cut lending rates in response to initiatives taken by the Reserve Bank of India in its 1997/98 (April-March) first half monetary policy announced on April 15.
Indian investors have in recent months shown a preference for income funds which invest predominantly in fixed income securities over growth funds which invest in equities.

Birla Income Plus has over 2.0 billion rupees invested in fixed income instruments. It has two plans - one offering dividend every six months and the other reinvesting dividends for long-term capital appreciation.
